title: People’s Mañanera September 28
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**A New Era for Workers: More Jobs, Higher Wages, and Greater Rights  
** “An additional 1.3 million people are employed thanks to Mexico’s new era
for workers,” President Claudia Sheinbaum noted. Mexico now has 60.7 million
people in the workforce; the minimum wage has risen by 154%; and the
transition to a 40-hour workweek is moving forward without reducing wages or
benefits.

**More Rights and Opportunities for the People  
** The Fourth Transformation (4T) is expanding rights: 199,000 digital
platform workers now have social security and healthcare coverage, and 1.7
million have protection against risks. In addition, the employment certificate
will protect 200,000 agricultural workers and the “Youth Building the Future”
program has already benefited 3.6 million young people.

**The 4T Restored Rights and Sovereignty  
** Sheinbaum stated that since 2018, with the election of the first 4T
administration, Mexico has been undergoing a new period of constitutional
reforms. The nature of Pemex and CFE as state-owned enterprises has been
strengthened, and pensions/stipends for senior citizens, the Well-being
Programs, and housing have been constitutionally enshrined as rights, along
with wage recovery.

**Ayotzinapa: The Investigation Remains Open  
** “New mechanisms, new investigative methodologies,” the President explained
regarding the lines of inquiry analyzing phone communications from the night
the 43 teacher-training students were forcibly disappeared. Sheinbaum
clarified that “nothing will be disclosed that has not already been disclosed
to their family members.”

**Mexico Calls for a Stronger UN  
** “The United Nations has been conspicuously absent in response to the
current international situation,” the President noted, referring to conflicts
such as Gaza, Ukraine, and Iran. She called for a more active UN in promoting
global peace, human rights, multilateralism, and equality among nations.
